subject: SIG: BCDR — regional recovery plan details and supporting artifacts
messages:

Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@evergreenhealth.com>

Subject: SIG follow-up — BCDR specifics we need

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the SIG packet this week. Our security team is doing a deeper pass focused on business continuity and disaster recovery (RTO/RPO, backups, regional failover). Can you provide specifics for the following items so we can close out our risk review?

- Target RTO & RPO for Redwood-hosted API endpoints and customer metadata (where applicable).
- Backup cadence and retention for production metadata and customer-owned artifacts.
- Cross-region failover approach (active-active vs warm-standby), expected DNS switch times, and any manual steps.
- Evidence from most recent DR drill (date, scope, screenshots or report).
- Any differences in SLAs / capabilities for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.

If possible, please include supporting artifacts (runbook excerpts, snapshot matrix, drill report). We have a deadline of EOD Tuesday for the SIG — appreciate anything you can share earlier.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Liu
Director, IT Security — Evergreen Health
alice.liu@evergreenhealth.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — BCDR specifics we need

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. I attached a short summary that addresses each bullet (redwood_sig_bcdr_summary.pdf) and a matrix for snapshot/retention. Quick answers inline below; Neha will follow with controls and drill evidence.

- RTO / RPO: Hosted API target RTO is 15 minutes for global control-plane failover; operational RTO for per-customer routing recovery is 30 minutes in typical scenarios. RPO for customer metadata is <1 minute for critical control-plane stores (near-real-time replication); daily backups retained for longer-term recovery.
- Backups: Incremental snapshots every 10 minutes for critical metadata, full snapshot nightly; short-term retention 30 days for snapshots, 90 days for analytics logs, 1 year for customer billing/audit archives (see snapshot_retention_matrix.csv).
- Failover approach: Hosted is warm-standby across two regions with automated health checks and DNS failover; Dedicated customers can opt into warm-standby or multi-region active routing (different pricing). Failover typically involves automated routing switch + connection draining; DNS propagation and client retries mean application-level recovery may take extra seconds–minutes.
- Drill evidence: Neha will share the last full drill report and dashboard screenshots.
- Differences by deployment: Private (on-prem/VPC) customers manage their own failover unless they opt into Redwood-managed DR; Dedicated customers have tighter SLA options.

I attached the summary and the retention matrix. If you want a short call next week to walk the runbook snippets, I can schedule Marissa and Neha.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Alice / Jordan,

Adding the technical detail that the SIG review team usually requests. Quick summary plus pointer to attached artifacts (runbook snippets and drill report).

1) RTO / RPO (by deployment):
- Hosted (default): RTO target 15 minutes for control-plane failover; operational RTO 30 minutes for in-flight session recovery under heavy load. RPO: best-effort continuous replication for control-plane data (typical RPO <1 minute for critical keys); event logs and telemetry replicated to object storage within ~5 minutes.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): RTO target 60–120 minutes for customer-isolated clusters if warm-standby not purchased; with warm-standby option RTO aligns closer to Hosted numbers. RPO depends on backup frequency configured per contract.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer-managed; Redwood provides guidance and automation bits but SLA depends on customer infrastructure and agreement.

2) Backup & retention specifics: incremental snapshots for metadata every 10 minutes; daily full backups to encrypted object storage. Retention tiers in attached matrix: 30-day rolling snapshots, 90-day short-term archive, 365-day long-term audit store (immutable snapshots stored with WORM-compatible settings where required). All backups encrypted at rest with customer KMS keys when configured.

3) Cross-region failover process (Hosted):
- Architecture: primary region active, secondary region warm-standby with continuous replication of control-plane and customer metadata.
- Trigger: automated health checks detect regional service degradation -> orchestrator initiates failover plan -> DNS failover and routing changes applied to edge proxies -> traffic shifts to standby region.
- Timeline: orchestrated steps take ~5–10 minutes; DNS propagation adds variable time depending on TTL (~up to 5 minutes with our low TTL defaults). Total service recovery target: 15 minutes.
- Manual steps: runbook excerpts show manual verification steps and rollback instructions; these are rarely needed but available in runbook_failover_snippets.md.

4) Evidence & testing cadence:
- Most recent full drill: 2025-03-30 (report attached: drill_report_20250330.pdf). Scope: control-plane failover + smoke tests across sample tenants; outcome: automated failover succeeded in 12 minutes; post-drill remediation items tracked.
- Test cadence: monthly smoke failovers (partial), quarterly tabletop reviews, annual full rehearsals. We provide drill summaries and relevant dashboard screenshots on request.

5) Controls / compliance notes:
- Backups and replication are covered under our SOC 2 Type II controls for change management, encryption, and backup procedures.
- For SIG artifacts we can provide runbook snippets, drill evidence screenshots (see attached), and policy references.

If you need specific screenshots from the March run or the raw metrics for the drill timeline, tell me which metrics you want (or we can schedule a shared screen).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
